summary: Petition under Sections 79(1) (c) and (f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulations 27, 33A and 33B of the CERC (Grant of Connectivity, Long-Term Access and MediumTerm Open Access in inter-State Transmission and related matters) Regulations, 2009, seeking recognition of force majeure events and issuance of appropriate orders. Order in Petition No. 66/MP/2023 _(b) Recognise that issuance of GIB Order on 19.04.2021 till the grant of approval for construction of overheard powerlines on 03.02.2023 is an event ‘akin to Force Majeure event’ for AMP Energy in terms of Transmission Agreement which prevented and delayed AMP Energy in construction of dedicated transmission lines;_ _(f) Pass any such other and further reliefs as this Commission deems just and proper in the nature and circumstances of the present case.”_ Order in Petition No. 66/MP/2023 Order in Petition No. 66/MP/2023 Order in Petition No. 66/MP/2023 4. After hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission admitted the Petition, and the parties were directed to file their respective replies and rejoinders. The Petitioner was directed to furnish the following clarification/details: - (i) Reasons for delay in approaching the Committee appointed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court on the GIB issue Order in Petition No. 66/MP/2023 5. The Respondents were also directed not to take any coercive action against the Petitioner, including encashment of the Bank Guarantee furnished by it to CTUIL for connectivity till the next date of hearing, provided the Petitioner keeps such BG alive. 6. The Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 18.04.2023, has filed the information called for. Replies to the Petition have been filed by NTPC and CTUIL - (a) There is no contractual relationship between the Petitioner and NTPC as no PPA has been entered into between the Petitioner and NTPC. - (c) As per clauses 3.20 and 3.24 of the RfS, the bid was to be kept valid for a period of 180 days from the bid opening date. Thereafter, such validity could be extended only with the consent of the bidder. The Petitioner had voluntarily extended the validity of its bid and Earnest Money Deposit. No fault or responsibility can be attributed to the NTPC for any consequences faced by the Petitioner on account of such extension. - (d) NTPC has not, at any stage, held out that the LoA would be issued to the Petitioner, or that the PPA would be executed so as to ensure that the scheduled date for commissioning of the Petitioner’s power plant could be achieved by 15.10.2022. Order in Petition No. 66/MP/2023 8. The Petitioner, in its rejoinder vide affidavit dated 06.06.2023 in response to the reply filed by NTPC, has mainly submitted that it is not seeking any relief against NTPC in the present Petition. At this stage, the Petitioner, having been put in an adverse financial position, cannot be held to be liable for non-issuance of the LoA by NTPC for its own wrong. Therefore, the event of non-issuance of the LoA by NTPC to the Petitioner falls within the meaning of events akin to Force Majeure. - a. The Petitioner was required to achieve the milestones prescribed in clause 9.3.1 of the Detailed Procedure and submit the proof thereof to the unified Powergrid/Respondent No.1 under the said two connectivity(s). Order in Petition No. 66/MP/2023 - f. GoI vide order dated 15.09.2021 extended SCODs of renewable energy projects, for which extension had already been granted in the case of the present Petitioner. 12. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner has completed the dedicated transmission line within the timeline given by the Hon’ble Supreme Court. Further, in response to the query of the Commission, learned counsel for CTUIL submitted that CTUIL is not proposing any action against Order in Petition No. 66/MP/2023 the Petitioner as the transition to GNA is in process. After hearing the parties, the Commission adjourned the matter and directed the Petitioner to furnish the following information: # ** Submission of Petitioner in Compliance with the RoP for the hearing dated ** 14. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition may be disposed of in terms of the amended Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022, and sought liberty to place on record the subsequent development in this regard. Learned counsel for the CTUIL submitted that since there is no issue of mismatch, the matter may be disposed of. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsels for the parties, the Commission directed the Petitioner to file its affidavit, as requested, and reserved the matter for order. # ** Submission of Petitioner in Compliance with the RoP for hearing dated 26.12.2024: ** Order in Petition No. 66/MP/2023 Order in Petition No. 66/MP/2023 survive, and we, therefore, find it appropriate to dispose of the instant Petition as having rendered infructuous.
